concepts.learning_objective: Define a map as a selective, symbolised and generalised representation of the earth at a reduced scale.
Distinguish a map from a sketch on the basis of scale and orientation.
Explain why scale and map projection are the first essentials of map making.
Explain map generalisation as selecting and simplifying content for the map's purpose.
Describe map design and map construction and production as steps of cartography.
Recall the early contributions of Mesopotamia, the Greeks and the Arabs to map making.
Trace the development of map making in India from the Vedic period to the Survey of India.

topics.title: Types of maps based on scale
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Maps Based on Scale

concepts.learning_objective: Identify cadastral and topographical maps as large-scale maps and state their purposes.
Identify wall maps and atlas maps as small-scale maps and compare their scales.

topics.title: Types of maps based on function
topics.ncert_sections: Types of Maps Based on Function

concepts.learning_objective: Identify relief, geological, climatic and soil maps as physical maps.
Identify political, population, economic and transportation maps as cultural maps.

topics.title: Uses of maps: measuring distance, direction and area

concepts.learning_objective: Choose suitable methods to measure straight and zigzag distances on a map.
Explain how directions are determined from the north base line using cardinal points.
Calculate area on a map using the method of squares and describe the polar planimeter.
